stem: Write the interval in interval notation.   x < 7

stem: The path of a shot put released at an angle of 35° can be modeled by y = −0.01x² + 0.6x + 6, where x is the horizontal distance (in feet) and y is the height (in feet). Find the coordinates of the vertex. What does the vertex represent?
title: Vertex in real life: a shot put
steps: The vertex is the highest point.

stem: The path of a basketball thrown at an angle of 45° can be modeled by y = −0.02x² + x + 6, where x is the horizontal distance (in feet) and y is the height (in feet). Find the coordinates of the vertex. What does the vertex represent?
title: Vertex in real life: a basketball
steps: The vertex is the highest point.

stem: The path of a diver is modeled by f(x) = −9x² + 9x + 3, where f(x) is the height of the diver (in meters) above the water and x is the horizontal distance (in meters) from the end of the diving board. Find the coordinates of the vertex. What does the vertex represent?
title: Vertex in real life: a diver
steps: The vertex is the highest point.

stem: The graph of which function has the same axis of symmetry as the graph of y = x² + 4x + 2?
title: Same axis of symmetry
steps: Check each choice the same way. This one matches.

stem: The graph of f(x) = 3x² + bx + c passes through (−3, 12) and (1, 12), and its minimum value is 0. Find the axis of symmetry, b, and c.
title: Challenge: find b and c from a minimum
steps: Two points with the same y are mirror images.

stem: The graph of f(x) = −2x² + bx + c passes through (1, −11) and (7, −11), and its maximum value is 7. Find the axis of symmetry, b, and c.

stem: Write an equation of the parabola.   vertex: (0, 0);  directrix: y = 6
title: Parabola from the vertex and directrix
steps: vertex (0, 0), directrix y = 6 → vertical axis, p = −6
p is the directed distance from the vertex to the focus. The directrix is on the other side, so the focus is 6 below: p is negative 6.
Use y equals x squared over 4 p.

stem: Write an equation of the parabola.   vertex: (0, 0);  focus: (3/4, 0)
title: Parabola from the vertex and focus
steps: The focus is on the x-axis, so the parabola opens sideways.
Use x equals y squared over 4 p.

stem: Write an equation of the parabola.   focus: (0, 3);  directrix: y = −3
title: Parabola from the focus and directrix
steps: The vertex is halfway between the focus and the directrix. The focus is 3 above it.

stem: Identify the focus, directrix, and axis of symmetry of the parabola.   y = (1/2)x²
title: Focus and directrix from y = ax²
steps: Match y equals 1 over 4 p times x squared.
The focus is p above the vertex, and the directrix is p below.

stem: Identify the focus, directrix, and axis of symmetry of the parabola.   6y² − 288x = 0
title: Focus and directrix: solve first
steps: Solve for the variable that isn't squared.

stem: Write an equation of the parabola with the given characteristics.   directrix: x = 11/2;  vertex: (3, 5)
title: Shifted parabola from the directrix and vertex
steps: The directrix x equals 11 halves is 5 halves to the right of the vertex, so the focus is 5 halves to the left.
Use x equals 1 over 4 p times y minus k squared, plus h.

stem: Write an equation of the parabola with the given characteristics.   focus: (−6, 1);  directrix: y = −5
title: Shifted parabola from the focus and directrix
steps: Halfway between y equals 1 and y equals negative 5 is negative 2.

stem: Identify the vertex, focus, and directrix of the parabola.   x = −3(y − 4)² + 2
title: Vertex, focus, and directrix of a shifted parabola
steps: Move p from the vertex for the focus, and the other way for the directrix.

stem: Which equation matches the graph?
title: Match a parabola to its equation
steps: vertex at the origin, opens left → y² = 4px, p < 0
Opening left means x is the squared-against variable and p is negative.
Check a point on the graph.

stem: Identify the focus, directrix, and axis of symmetry of the parabola. Then graph it: place the vertex, then one more point.   x = −(1/16)y²
title: Graph a parabola with a focus
steps: Pick y equals 4: x is negative 1.

stem: A parabolic reflector has a focal length of 2 inches and an aperture width of 10 inches. The vertex is at (0, 0) and the reflector opens to the right, so its equation is x = (1/(4p))y². What is the depth of the reflector (the value of x at the edge of the aperture)? Round to the nearest hundredth.
title: Parabola in real life: depth of a reflector

stem: The cross section (with units in inches) of a parabolic satellite dish can be modeled by the equation y = (1/20)x². How far is the focus from the vertex of the cross section?
title: Parabola in real life: a satellite dish
steps: Compare with y equals 1 over 4 p times x squared.
The focus is p from the vertex: 5 inches.

stem: The cross section (with units in inches) of a parabolic spotlight can be modeled by the equation x = (1/38)y². How far is the focus from the vertex of the cross section?
title: Parabola in real life: a spotlight
steps: Compare with x equals 1 over 4 p times y squared.
The focus is 9.5 inches from the vertex.

stem: A parabola has focus (4, 1) and directrix y = 3. Find its vertex and the value of a when the equation is written as y = a(x − h)² + k.
title: Challenge: from focus and directrix to vertex form
steps: Halfway between y equals 1 and y equals 3.
The focus is below, so it opens down.

steps: Halfway between gives the maximum: a 10 by 10 square.
